extraction.name: CommonsenseQA
extraction.description: A challenging new multiple-choice question answering dataset targeting commonsense knowledge. It contains 12,247 questions generated from ConceptNet relations, where crowd-workers author questions that distinguish between related target concepts.
extraction.creator: Alon Talmor, Jonathan Herzig, Nicholas Lourie, Jonathan Berant
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was generated by extracting triplets from ConceptNet, grouping them into question sets, and then using Amazon Mechanical Turk crowdworkers to formulate and validate questions. Additional distractors were added by crowdworkers, and textual context was added by querying a search engine to retrieve web snippets.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: ConceptNet knowledge base and web snippets retrieved via search engine.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Crowdworkers authored three questions per subgraph (one per target concept), added two additional distractors per question, and then a disjoint group of workers verified question quality by marking questions as unanswerable or selecting the right answer. Each question was verified by 2 workers, and only questions verified by at least one worker that answered correctly were used.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Questions were verified by 2 workers, and only questions verified by at least one worker that answered correctly were kept; this filtering removed 15% of the questions.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 2 workers per question verification; 3 questions authored per subgraph
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: ConceptNet rules/edge filtering were used to extract subgraphs and select one distractor from answer concepts with the same relation in ConceptNet; Google search was used to collect textual snippets for each question and candidate answer.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper notes that commonsense benchmarks can be affected by distributional biases and annotation artifacts, and that models may exploit these rather than true understanding.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is limited to commonsense question answering based on ConceptNet and does not require additional information; the paper also frames commonsense QA as a difficult challenge and notes that similar benchmarks have scalability issues.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for commonsense question answering benchmark use, including evaluating models' commonsense reasoning; the paper positions it as a larger-scale test set for such evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For each question concept and relation, three different triplets were grouped into question sets to create semantically similar answer concepts, and crowdworkers added additional distractors to the multiple-choice questions.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Triplets were filtered from ConceptNet by removing concepts with more than four words or not in English, and by filtering triplets where the edit distance between c1 and c2 was too low.
